mutant.description: the order names no mutant; the suite carries its own negative arms: the pinned original wrapper run side by side with the new one (same exit code and output once the block's lines are removed, also with both tools crashing), one switch present with the other check in WARN, an expired notice, a targeted apply that does not name the guarded resource, a CLOSED-BOTH call, the applying seat's own open deploy, a project placed on this box, TIER2 with no task order, a carried file outside another box's write set, a push that deploys nothing, a sentinel naming the shared root but no carried file
mutant.expected: each negative arm reads clear or unchanged where its positive arm reads hit or refused
mutant.observed: 87 of 87 cases pass, positive and negative arms in the same run

determinism.method: N/A: the tools are pure reads of files and git objects; the suite builds its own scratch repository and takes the time from --now

declared_exclusions.item: a real terraform plan or apply, an AWS call, a real deploy, a push, and the creation of any of the five enforce files (org/mcp/seat-gates.enforce and the four seat-gates.<check>.<wrapper>.enforce)
declared_exclusions.reason: the order forbids all of them; the wrappers were exercised only through --dry-seat-gates and as far as a scratch tree's missing halt-gate file and a STUB deploy core that only prints; the switch files were created only in scratch trees or in a temp directory named by OPAL_SEAT_GATES_ENFORCE_DIR; a byte copy of the REAL safe_deploy_core.py is imported by the helper, never run
written by other cells and absent from this worktree; apply-who-check.py resolves the kind module, then file, then built-in, and the suite exercises all three sources with fixtures
